question: Does the box shift every character by +5 and append W regardless of case and character class, or does it treat uppercase/lowercase/digits/spaces differently?
expect: If the model is right, outputs will be 'fW','FW','~W','_W','5W','>W','%W','&W','fghW','FGHW'. Any deviation reveals per-class handling (e.g., case preserved, digits shifted differently, spaces unchanged), which would explain the 'Hello World function lazy' and 'bananaUPPER' mismatches.

question: Does the +5 shift wrap around at the end of the printable ASCII range (e.g. '~', '}', '|', '\'), or does it produce characters beyond '~' as plain ord+5 would?
expect: Plain ord+5 predicts '\u0083W', '\u0082W', '\u0081W', '\u0080W', '|W', '{W', 'zW', 'yW', '\u0083\u0083\u0083W', '\u007f\u007f\u007fW'. If instead the box wraps within printable ASCII (e.g. '~'->'#' or similar), the outputs will differ. This tests whether the shift is a naive codepoint add or a bounded/wrapping shift, which ordinary inputs containing 'w'..'~' would expose.

question: Does the box apply the +5 shift and W-suffix to ordinary multi-word sentences containing punctuation, digits, and mixed case, or does it do something else for longer/typical inputs?
expect: If the model is right, outputs will be each character shifted +5 with W appended: 'Ymj%vn|hp%gtw{ %ktsW', 'Mjqqt1%\twqi&W', 'yjxy678%fghW', 'Ifyf%Xnhjshj%656W', 'f%g%hW', 'RnxjiXfxj%fsi%xufhjxW', 'tsj%ywd%yjwjjW', '}%?%}%6W', 'HfrifXfxiBsqiW', 'jsi W'. Any deviation (e.g., punctuation handled differently, no suffix, or different shift) would reveal a rule the current model misses for ordinary sentence-like inputs.

question: Does the box append exactly one 'W' at the end even when the input already ends in 'W' or contains repeated trailing characters, i.e. is the suffix unconditional?
expect: If the model is right, each output is the +5-shifted input followed by a single 'W' (e.g. 'W'->'\W', 'WW'->'\\WW', 'abcW'->'fgh\W'). Any deviation (no suffix, or suffix doubled) would show the W-append is conditional on the last character and refine the model.
